zero-inference: Streams CPU/NVMe weights to the GPU layer by layer, amortizing transfers with prefetch and large batches. A throughput-oriented offload precedent predating recent coding agents.
fiddler: A small-batch Mixtral prototype that computes nonresident experts on the CPU and transfers activations, illustrating the alternative to moving expert weights.
flash-moe: An AI-assisted Qwen/Metal implementation that streams quantized experts from SSD. It reduces active experts from 10 to 4, so its execution is approximate.
flexllmgen: An OPT throughput runtime using GPU/CPU/disk placement, cross-microbatch weight reuse and overlapped transfers; not a general low-latency serving result.
ktransformers: A heterogeneous MoE backend that uses ISA-specific CPU kernels and NUMA placement for memory-heavy experts while retaining shared GPU serving infrastructure.
moe-infinity: Offloads experts across memory tiers with activation-aware caching and trace-based prefetch. A residency-policy precedent; the public implementation differs from the paper system.
strata: A selected-Qwen CPU/GPU engine combining hot-expert residency with tiered KV management. Some paths use approximate expert skipping; AI authorship is not established.
vllm: A general-engine comparison for VibeQwen and a serving foundation reused by Radiance, with paged KV, prefix sharing and continuous batching.
bitnet-cpp: An engine for compatible ternary models using packed kernels, lookup tables and shape specialization. Losslessness concerns the existing ternary representation, not arbitrary floating-point models.
deepcompressor: Calibrates low-bit quantization and SVDQuant decompositions and exports weights for backends such as Nunchaku. Model preparation and simulated evaluation are distinct from runtime acceleration.
exllamav3: An EXL3-centered runtime coupling low-bit execution, quantized paged KV and shape-qualified decode paths; numerical behavior and coverage depend on configuration.
ik-llama: A deep llama.cpp fork extending packed formats, CPU IQK kernels and CUDA dispatch while retaining general-engine compatibility.
marlin: An INT4 execution component referenced by ExLlamaV3, combining offline repacking with load/dequantization/matmul pipelining; not a complete inference service.
nunchaku: A diffusion backend that fuses SVDQuant low-bit matrix multiplication with low-rank branches. Quantization, offload and cache gains require separate attribution.
qtip: Trellis-coded weights with matching matrix-vector kernels, referenced by ExLlamaV3. The public interactive path lacks fusion used for the main reported timings.
sageattention: Reusable attention kernels combining outlier smoothing with hardware-specific INT8/FP8 paths. Operator speed and quality checks do not substitute for full video-pipeline validation.
fastvideo: An integrated video runtime owning model implementations, loading and staged denoising, with optional sparsity, parallelism and offload. Sparse or distilled paths may change the model.
powerinfer: A CPU/GPU runtime placing frequently activated neurons on GPU and using predictors for sparse execution. Requires compatible sparse models, not arbitrary dense weights.
turbodiffusion: A video stack combining low-precision/sparse attention, timestep-distilled weights and optional quantized layers. Separate model and step-count changes from implementation gains.
sglang: A shared serving foundation for systems such as KTransformers, with radix-prefix KV reuse and cache-aware scheduling. Reuse depends on compatible prefixes and configuration.
inferix: A semi-autoregressive world-model runtime separating persistent generation KV, VAE chunking and streamed video output. This execution redesign does not establish AI-assisted construction.
tensorrt-llm: A general-engine reference for VibeQwen combining NVIDIA kernels, chunked-context scheduling, dynamic batching and paged KV; comparisons must match precision and workload.
videosys: An integrated video execution reference combining type-specific attention reuse with dynamic sequence parallelism. Attention broadcast is approximate and model support is bounded.
xdit: A distributed DiT framework combining sequence-parallel schemes and patch pipelines. Earlier-step feature reuse differs from exact synchronous execution; supported combinations are constrained.
tvm: The compiler foundation beneath MLC LLM, providing graph transformations, tensor scheduling and target code generation. Model and serving policies remain higher-level responsibilities.
draw-things: Public Swift model graphs, samplers and hardware execution components for local generation, including approximate TeaCache reuse. Their availability does not establish that the entire product is open source.
dwarfstar: An explicitly AI-assisted native runtime for selected models, combining resident non-routed state with bounded SSD expert caching; model and backend support is deliberately limited.
edge-dit: A ggml-based DiT runtime owning graphs, component residency and staged offload, with quantization and tiled VAE execution for constrained memory. Cache and backend support vary by model.
flash-linear-attention: Linear-attention and recurrent-state kernels reused by ExLlamaV3, with chunked prefill and state updates for compatible architectures; not equivalent replacements for arbitrary softmax attention.
flash-attention: Reusable IO-aware attention kernels with fused reductions and KV-update interfaces. Exact mathematical attention does not imply bitwise identity or whole-system speedup.
flashinfer: Selects or generates kernels by precision, head geometry and cache layout, including paths reused by MoE-Infinity; not a standalone inference server.
halogen-flash: A model-and-chip-specific Qwen binary with mixed precision, paged n-gram lookup and dedicated expert execution. Its closed core limits implementation inspection.
iris: A native image pipeline in C with Metal/CPU kernels, mapped weights and text-encoder release after conditioning, illustrating ownership of the graph and its execution.
lightx2v: A video execution stack combining model-specific paths, storage contracts and double-buffered weight loading. Attribute quantization, distilled weights and lightweight VAE changes separately.
llama-cpp: A shared native foundation for specialized forks, with GGUF loading, GGML graphs and backend quantized kernels; useful for distinguishing inherited infrastructure from execution changes.
magnitude: The reviewed Metal/MLX path maps typed operations to compatible kernel plans and emits specialized fused entry points. This evidence does not cover other backends.
mflux: Native selected-image-model implementations on MLX, with load-time quantization and adapter merging; a useful contrast between framework-level ports and deeper execution redesign.
mirage: Compiles an explicitly assembled LLM task graph into persistent CUDA execution with GPU workers scheduling computation and communication across decode steps; coverage depends on implemented graphs and tasks.
mlc-llm: A TVM-based model compiler and MLCEngine runtime, fusing operations and specializing small-batch computation and KV kernels; illustrates portability trade-offs in compiled deployment.
tensorrt: Builds NVIDIA engines around shape profiles and kernel tactics and underlies Edge-LLM. The public repository exposes plugins/examples, not the complete optimizer and runtime core.
onediff: Adapts diffusion components to OneFlow/Nexfort compilation and graph reuse. Public adapter code does not establish visibility of every compiler core.
stable-fast: Incrementally specializes Diffusers through TorchScript tracing, fused operators and optional CUDA graphs; numerical behavior and graph compatibility require workload-specific checks.
stable-diffusion-cpp: Native ggml-based image/video loading, conditioning, sampling and component placement, with quantization and VAE tiling. Optional approximate caching is separate from the native rewrite.
tensorfold: A native Zig runtime for qualified models and formats, using packed-layout contracts and Metal/CUDA paths; projection fusion requires compatible packing.
agentcompile: Uses an LLM to select bounded CUDA templates and generate fused kernels for a runtime. Reviewed generic verification/timing paths contain skipped checks and placeholders.
akg-agents: Builds and migrates accelerator operators through multi-agent search, code generation, backend validation and profiling; a kernel-construction workflow, not a complete inference engine.
fastkernels: Integrates candidate operators into deployment-shaped pipelines, checking kernel numerics/timing and end-to-end outputs/latency; separates local tolerance tests from model behavior.
kernelagent: Partitions PyTorch programs into fusible subgraphs, generates Triton kernels and composes forward execution using correctness and hardware feedback. Finite tests do not prove general correctness.
kernelbench: Compiles generated kernels, compares randomized inputs against PyTorch references and times passing candidates; evaluates construction tasks, not deployed-engine gains.
metainfer: Orchestrates coding agents to construct deployment-specific servers and checks fixed correctness/performance contracts, connecting to VibeQwen. Finite prompt checks do not establish numerical equivalence.
sol-engine: An agent-guided video optimization workflow integrating model-specific fusion, state reuse, approximate caches and sparse attention with visual checks; each change needs separate validation and attribution.
tilelang: A kernel language used by Atrex, compiling tiled programs through target layouts and software pipelining. Its generated kernels are distinct from a complete model runtime.
triton: A code-generation foundation for KernelAgent and others, specializing tiled kernels and launch configurations by target/signature/constants; it does not own model loading or service validation.
ninfer: A native selected-Qwen runtime for one RTX 5090, owning execution, KV/CUDA graphs and request/cache management. Agent instruction files do not establish AI authorship.
splash: A native Apple Silicon serving stack with model-specific Metal kernels, draft verification and prefix reuse. Disclosed agent assistance concerns kernels, not authorship of the entire engine.
llamampere: A deep llama.cpp fork combining Ampere verification kernels, MTP drafts and compressed KV while retaining shared serving. Separate post-trained models and quantization from engine contributions.
gufo: A selected-model C++/HIP stack for AMD Strix Halo, owning kernels, batching and continuation caching while reusing upstream components; quality qualification is model-specific.
lily: A Rust/Metal runtime for one quantized Qwen checkpoint, owning prefill/decode and prefix caching. Its text-only, greedy, nonstreaming interface makes the compatibility trade-off explicit.
lithos-metal: Compiles typed model graphs into layer-fused and conventional kernels, using Metal indirect commands and GPU-resident draft state; backend coverage and fused numerics remain qualified.
saragossa: A single-user Apple Silicon runtime for selected text/speech models, with Rust/Metal execution, resident decode state, buffers and prefix snapshots backed by regression comparisons.
turbo-fieldfare: A Gemma runtime for memory-limited Apple Silicon using bounded expert-read slots and chunked prefill, with documented accepted and discarded construction experiments.
tuff: A Swift/Metal streaming-runtime fork adding model-specific forward paths, bounded expert loading and a separate service, illustrating adaptation across MoE families.
colibri: Architecture-specific C engines sharing selected components, with resident dense state and streamed experts. Backend, quantization and approximation choices need per-engine qualification.
ane-cpp: Compiles Qwen convolution programs for ANE while the CPU handles normalization, attention and KV state, informed by hardware probes and kept/discarded experiments.
swiftlet: An explicitly AI-assisted Swift/Metal reconstruction of selected Qwen hybrid-MoE paths, combining expert containers, caching and native state with documented reference checks.
swiftlm: Reworks expert reads, asynchronous I/O and generation synchronization in MLX Swift and maintained forks to explicitly stream oversized MoE models from SSD.
anemll-flash-llama: A llama.cpp fork with expert sidecars, slot mapping and layer-major prefill. Optional reduced top-k and shared-expert-only modes change model computation.
uzu: A reusable edge engine combining Rust model blocks, native Metal dispatch, model conversion and generated bindings. Source availability alone does not establish AI authorship.
pmetal: An Apple Silicon training/inference SDK combining model implementations, native inference bridges and device operators, illustrating specialized execution within a broader ecosystem.
metalchat: A C++/Metal native generation path built from tensor, layer and model abstractions; an adjacent reusable-framework example whose generation tests do not establish full quality coverage.
basert: Public conversion tools, C APIs and bindings around a proprietary native engine. The closed execution core limits kernel and performance evidence to author documentation.
anemll: Splits, quantizes and converts models into stateful Core ML packages with Swift/Python orchestration; actual ANE placement remains a Core ML decision.
ane-lm: A direct predecessor to ane.cpp, connecting Qwen ANE kernels and CPU operations through a compile cache; constrained by private interfaces and limited model coverage.
coreml-llm-cli: A Llama 2 host runtime orchestrating chunked Core ML execution, KV state and IOSurface buffers; a compiled-model integration precedent to ANEMLL.
hipengine: A selected-AMD execution stack with a Python host, HIP/C++ model kernels, shared KV and continuous batching, without PyTorch in the inference path.
vte: A consumer-RDNA3 stack owning GGUF parsing, template-generated HIP kernels, VRAM management and decode-graph replay around memory and driver constraints.
zinc: A Zig runtime owning model loading, forward graphs, KV and serving over native Vulkan/HIP and other backends; each device path needs separate qualification.
imp: A C++/CUDA engine for RTX 5090-class devices, owning model execution, paged KV, graph scheduling and serving. The author explicitly discloses end-to-end coding-agent implementation.
memra: A Rust host connecting ahead-of-time CUDA kernels and model-specific programs, explicitly managing quantization, KV and multi-GPU placement with model/device-specific numerical checks.
kipp: A C11 stack owning strict checkpoint loading, tokenization, model execution, paged KV and batched serving through isolated Metal/CUDA backends.
vllm-radiance: Retains vLLM serving while rebuilding RDNA4 paths with pinned patches and HIP kernels; low-bit arithmetic and speculative execution require separate equivalence checks.
ninfer-3090: An NInfer fork adapted to a 24 GB RTX 3090 through new SM86 quantized kernels, memory planning and replay state, beyond a compile-target change.
infernix: An explicitly AI-assisted NInfer fork combining GPU hot-expert caching, CPU miss computation, overlapped PCIe transfers and NVMe storage.
ciru-runtime: A llama.cpp-derived runtime coupling expert paging, specialized kernels, sparse attention and speculative-state fixes to specific model formats and release builds.
gufo-rdma: Extends Gufo across two Strix Halo hosts, using tensor partitioning, RDMA collectives and mirrored requests to synchronize execution and speculative state.
llaminar: Builds native model graphs and device plans, placing stages and experts across CPU/NVIDIA/AMD devices with explicit heterogeneous communication.
strix-llama-cpp: A llama.cpp fork with Strix Halo fusion kernels and speculative-state management. Optional speculative prefill is approximate; accepting agent contributions does not establish AI authorship.
rocmfpx: A llama.cpp downstream co-designing AMD quantization blocks, conversion policies and matching kernels; accuracy must be qualified per recipe.
hybrimoe: A KTransformers-based combination of CPU/GPU expert scheduling, prefetch and caching; a precedent for placement and movement in models exceeding VRAM.
cactus: A mobile runtime lowering supported model components into its own graph operations, ARM/Metal kernels and quantized state; general conversion coverage remains limited.
fastflowlm: Model-family host runtimes managing AMD NPU tensors, weights and decode streams with shape-matched kernels; original flm engines ship as prebuilt libraries.
zllm: Rust model/backend-specific loading, execution and state management covering vision-language, image generation and video restoration; each combination has its own support boundary.
needle: Pairs sliceable-attention models and quantized weights with platform-native engines. Model and packaging code is public, but the distributed C++ engine implementation is not.
tensorrt-edge-llm: An edge-deployment reference combining ONNX export and TensorRT compilation with C++ decoding, KV and multimodal embedding management.
brain: Rust model implementations sharing a WGSL backend, including vision-language/video component-residency decisions; a model list does not establish full validation of every path.
hilum-engine: A llama.cpp/GGML mobile integration for Adreno/Vulkan and Metal, adjusting shader dispatch, allocation and device parameters.
qwen-asr-c: A C reconstruction of Qwen3-ASR preprocessing, encoder, autoregressive decoding and chunked streaming state, with explicit CPU and optional GPU responsibilities.
qwen3-tts-c: Rebuilds the Qwen3-TTS talker, code predictor and waveform decoder in C, with reference checks and measurement corrections; engineering task files do not establish AI authorship.
qingming-qwen3-tts: Separate native Qwen3-TTS paths for 24 GB RX 7900 XTX and RTX 4090 devices, explicitly partitioning resident generation and streaming-decoder resources.
voxgen: A Rust VoxCPM2 reconstruction with direct Vulkan buffer/shader management and incremental PCM state; RDNA3 configurations have separate tuning and qualification scopes.
parakeet-ggml: Ports NeMo speech features, encoder/decoder graphs and cache-aware streaming sessions to C++/ggml, with GGUF conversion and reference-parity fixtures.
parakeet-axiom: A C++ Parakeet reconstruction on axiom, owning encoder/decoder and streaming caches while reusing CPU/MPSGraph tensor backends; local checks are not end-to-end results.
aria: A C Stable Audio 3 pipeline owning conditioning, diffusion, sampling and audio decoding, with disclosed LLM assistance and controlled reference tests; construction cost remains unknown.
vla-simd: Native C++/CPU-SIMD operators, GGUF loading and action inference for selected vision-language-action policies. Throughput and numerical tests do not establish closed-loop safety.
hearth: A Rust SD pipeline owning model graphs, samplers and dependency-ordered execution while reusing CubeCL/wgpu kernels and device access.
brodiffusion: A C++ image runtime owning loading, diffusion pipelines and samplers, with shape/state-qualified denoising-graph replay over a reused brotensor backend.
stable-diffusion-rs: Rust diffusion models and samplers with documented Candle-to-MLX migration and reference checks; agent task instructions do not establish AI authorship.
minimax-h3-mlx: An MLX reconstruction of joint MiniMax-H3 audio/video diffusion, precomputing timestep conditioning and staging component residency; quantization mainly affects capacity.
vidax: Ports video graphs and checkpoint layouts to JAX/Flax TPU meshes, explicitly composing tensor/sequence sharding, attention kernels and component placement.
telefuser: Co-designs generation stages and streaming scheduling, separating resident session state from GPU execution leases with backpressure. Optional cache, sparsity and precision modes change semantics.
streamdiffusion-v2: Reorganizes causal Wan chunked denoising, stage scheduling and distributed KV ownership. Causal/distilled checkpoints and optional lightweight decoding change the comparison target.
saient-quartz: Image generation on a custom Rust tensor backend with native Wan work in progress. Demonstrated mobile Wan uses a separate C++ companion, not the native Rust path.
whisper-cpp: An established native Whisper/ggml speech runtime with converted weights and multiple backends; a historical reference, not evidence of recent AI-driven construction savings.
whisperkit: Swift orchestration of Core ML speech preprocessing, encoder/decoder, caches and segmentation, illustrating the execution boundary between compiled models and their host runtime.
diffusion-rs: FLUX loading, sampling, quantization and residency on a reusable Rust tensor layer; a reuse/offload reference without inferred coding-agent authorship.
streamdiffusion: Reorganizes Diffusers into StreamBatch with residual guidance, input filtering and optional compilation; approximate guidance and skipped frames change outputs or workload.
ncu-report-skill: Extracts Nsight Compute metrics and source-level stalls to connect measured bottlenecks with candidate optimizations; a diagnosis workflow, not an inference engine.
atrex-kernel-agent: Runs coding agents in isolated worktrees to generate operator kernels, applying numerical/performance gates and revising with profiler feedback and retrieved knowledge; not a complete engine.
atrex-bench: Production-sourced operator tasks, reference programs and shape generators with separate agent-visible inputs and evaluator metadata; checks compilation/numerics/timing, not whole-stack acceleration.
kernelwiki: Indexes kernel optimization experience, documents and upstream changes by hardware and symptom, retaining artifact provenance; a searchable knowledge resource, not a runtime.
ane-field-guide: MIL/ANE probes and CPU-reference checks recording kept/discarded M3 Max experiments whose findings inform ane.cpp; a knowledge resource, not another engine.
